description: Two iterations modeling a LAYERED failure: a parse error hides a type error which hides an ownership error. Exercises both ends of the loop — two machine-applicable classes and one that requires the LLM to re-reason from prose.

responses.note: First attempt, carrying three mistakes that surface in LAYERS — which is the point of this fixture. `&&` (Rust habit) is a parse error and masks everything behind it; `karac fix` now resolves it in place (B-2026-08-01-25). Only then does typecheck reveal `i64 as char` (E_INT_AS_CHAR — NOT machine-applicable, the LLM must re-reason and switch to a byte loop) and a use-after-move on the sort key (machine-applicable). One iteration cannot see all three.
Second attempt after reading E_INT_AS_CHAR: the lowercaser is rewritten to work in bytes, since `u8 as char` is legal where `i64 as char` is not. This is the reference solution.
